| [CASE-062](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-062.md) v2 | Simplified texts for restricted and full readers | A constructed study, built on documented halves. | [CASE-355](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-355.md) | Registered evaluation in synthetic organizations | [LEAD-017](../../../record/leads.d/LEAD-017.md) asked for A13's three organizations of matched behaviour and different endorsement relations, and a measure of registration that does not read the experimenter's setting ([QUESTION-270](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-270.md)'s second requirement). In small numpy simulations an outcome's hedonic value declines progressively from +1 to −0.8. A consummatory process H evaluates it, and pursuit P keeps choosing it at a calibrated rate of 0.6 in all three organizations. In the denied organization H's evaluation is written into the organization's record and has no authority over pursuit. In the accommodating one it is written and has authority beyond a tolerance that reciprocal compensation widens. In the unregistered one it is never written. The record is mixed by an unknown rotation and noisy. The measure perturbs H's evaluation at random, as a hotspot probe would, and asks whether the record responds, holding fixed the outcome, the action and P's learned value. With thresholds set on one seed, on 200 held-out agents per organization it called every registered agent registered and no unregistered one (AUC 1.0). It was not fooled by a decoy record carrying the evaluation's physiological cause by another route (2% false calls, against 77% for the passive reading), nor by an evaluation that steers pursuit directly, bypassing the record (1.5%). It missed weak registration (gain 0.1 to 0.25) in 60% of agents. The authority probe told accommodation from denial in 43% of agents at 4.5% false calls. A stipulated model, one size, one probe protocol. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
